react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm analysis of the 11 differentially abundant metabolites using mummichog (m/z-direct) against the human_mfn empirical-compound network revealed six significantly perturbed pathways (FDR-adjusted p < 0.05). The strongest signal converged on carbohydrate-related metabolism: Sialic acid metabolism (p = 0.0047), Hexose phosphorylation (p = 0.0047), Phosphatidylinositol phosphate metabolism (p = 0.0047), Galactose metabolism (p = 0.0166), Starch and Sucrose Metabolism (p = 0.0119), and Glycerophospholipid metabolism (p = 0.0119). Driver metabolites driving these hits are D-glucose (β-D-glucose, KEGG:C00221), sucrose (KEGG:C00089), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), galactinol (α-D-galactosyl-(1→3)-1D-myo-inositol, KEGG:C01235), galactitol (KEGG:C01697), glycerol (KEGG:C00116), and ethanolamine (KEGG:C00189) — all confirmed as members of the overlapping hits lists. The empirical-compound layer from mummichog further mapped D-glucose to mass features row1/row2, sucrose and galactinol to rows 11–18, myo-inositol and glycerol to rows 7–10/13–14, and ethanolamine to rows 9–10. Separately, 2-methoxyestradiol (KEGG:C05302, a known anti-mitotic estrogen derivative) was captured as an empirical hit in mass features row3–row4 mapped to the androgen/estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism pathway. Squalene (KEGG:C00751) and inosine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate (KEGG:C05768) did not register significant pathway enrichment but were confirmed as distinct empirical mass features. InChIKey reconciliation confirmed all 11 compounds resolve to unique first-block hashes with no structural conflicts, validating that namespace ambiguity did not drive any false-positive pathway associations.

Mummichog (m/z-direct, empirical-compound network) returned nine significant pathway hits driven by six of the ten resolvable input metabolites. The top hit, Galactose metabolism (p = 0.017), is supported by four driver compounds: myo-inositol (C00137), sucrose (C00089), galactinol (C01235), and glucose (C00221), with galactitol (C01697) also mapping to the pathway's hit-list. Starch and Sucrose Metabolism (p = 0.015) shares sucrose, galactinol, glucose, myo-inositol, and glycerol (C00116) as inputs, reflecting the disaccharide and hexose overlap between the two carbohydrate pathways. Glycerophospholipid Metabolism (p = 0.015) is anchored by myo-inositol, glycerol, and ethanolamine (C00189), the latter being a canonical head-group precursor in phospholipid biosynthesis. Phosphatidylinositol phosphate metabolism (p = 0.008) is driven by myo-inositol and glucose, consistent with inositol's role in PI signaling and its hexose-phase partner in central carbon flow. A borderline hit in Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism (p = 0.085) captures 2-methoxyestradiol (C05302), the methylated derivative of 17β-estradiol. Dopamine (C03758) did not enrich in any mummichog pathway but is biologically linked to catecholamine and neuroactive-ligand networks outside the primary carbohydrate/lipid signal. One input metabolite, inosine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate (KEGG:C05768), could not be resolved to a valid structure via InChIKey (SBJVDTBACUMFFD resolved to coproporphyrinogen I) and was excluded from enrichment. The convergent finding across galactose, disaccharide, and glycerophospholipid axes points to a coordinated shift in sugar utilization and membrane-lipid remodeling under the treatment condition.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Mummichog m/z-direct pathway analysis of the 11 differentially abundant metabolites returned 15 enriched pathways (p < 0.05), with carbohydrate and sugar-nucleotide metabolism dominating the top ranks. The strongest signal (p = 0.00319) was shared by three tightly connected pathways: Sialic acid metabolism (KEGG:hsa00601), Hexose phosphorylation (KEGG:hsa00010 module), and Phosphatidylinositol phosphate metabolism (KEGG:hsa00562). Glycerophospholipid metabolism (KEGG:hsa00564) and Starch and Sucrose Metabolism (KEGG:hsa00500) ranked just below (p = 0.00748), followed by Galactose metabolism (KEGG:hsa00052, p = 0.00899). Fructose and mannose metabolism, glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, and the pentose phosphate pathway each appeared with p ≤ 0.05. An estrogen-related pathway (Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism) was marginally significant (p = 0.084). Notably, KEGG compound C05768 ('Inosine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate') could not be reconciled by InChIKey: the input InChIKey SBJVDTBACUMFFD maps to a cyclic phosphate species, while KEGG C05768 resolves via lookup_chebi to coproporphyrinogen I (WIUGGJKHYQIGNH) — a connectivity-level conflict indicating a database annotation error for this entry. The driver metabolites anchoring the top carbohydrate pathways are myo-Inositol (C00137), D-Glucose (C00221), Sucrose (C00089), Galactitol (C01697), and Galactinol (C01235), all present in the mummichog hits_kegg_ids lists. Ethanolamine (C00189) anchors the glycerophospholipid hit, and 2-Methoxyestradiol (C05302) is the driver for the marginal steroid pathway. RaMP, FELLA, MetaboAnalystR, and SSPA returned empty results for this KEGG-only input set, consistent with their stricter ID-resolution requirements. The convergent signal across six carbon-metabolism pathways suggests a broad disruption of hexose handling and sugar-donor pools in the treatment condition, with secondary involvement of membrane lipid remodelling and a weak estrogen biosynthesis imprint.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm analysis of the 11 differentially abundant metabolites using mummichog (m/z-direct) against the human_mfn empirical-compound network revealed six significantly perturbed pathways (FDR-adjusted p < 0.05). The strongest signal converged on carbohydrate-related metabolism: Sialic acid metabolism (p = 0.0047), Hexose phosphorylation (p = 0.0047), Phosphatidylinositol phosphate metabolism (p = 0.0047), Galactose metabolism (p = 0.0166), Starch and Sucrose Metabolism (p = 0.0119), and Glycerophospholipid metabolism (p = 0.0119). Driver metabolites driving these hits are D-glucose (β-D-glucose, KEGG:C00221), sucrose (KEGG:C00089), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), galactinol (α-D-galactosyl-(1→3)-1D-myo-inositol, KEGG:C01235), galactitol (KEGG:C01697), glycerol (KEGG:C00116), and ethanolamine (KEGG:C00189) — all confirmed as members of the overlapping hits lists. The empirical-compound layer from mummichog further mapped D-glucose to mass features row1/row2, sucrose and galactinol to rows 11–18, myo-inositol and glycerol to rows 7–10/13–14, and ethanolamine to rows 9–10. Separately, 2-methoxyestradiol (KEGG:C05302, a known anti-mitotic estrogen derivative) was captured as an empirical hit in mass features row3–row4 mapped to the androgen/estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism pathway. Squalene (KEGG:C00751) and inosine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate (KEGG:C05768) did not register significant pathway enrichment but were confirmed as distinct empirical mass features. InChIKey reconciliation confirmed all 11 compounds resolve to unique first-block hashes with no structural conflicts, validating that namespace ambiguity did not drive any false-positive pathway associations.
